name: MorningPremonition
source:
My wife was sleeping peacefully next to me. I smoothed a curl that clung to her neck and kissed her on the cheek. Lazily, she woke and smiled. 
 
 We moved for a while, kissing and generally enjoying ourselves. Eventually she sat up. She was beautiful like this. Hair wild, eyes bright. Naked in bed. 
 
 I scanned her form slowly, enjoying her curves and the look on her face as she watched me. Her slender neck, sloping shoulders, perfect breasts, glowing stomach.... Wait what? 
 
 My heart sank. I strained my eyes, trying to convince myself that what I saw was just a trick of the light. 
 
 There was no mistake. 
 
 My wife was pregnant, and the child inside her would one day be my undoing. My family gift, knowing what person or thing would kill us, has never been more of a curse. 
 
 `` Honey?'' My wife's concerned voice breaks through my thoughts. I force a smile on my face. 
 
 `` Yes dear?''

Perspective: The Unborn Child (Referred to as "Little One")

In the quiet recesses of darkness, I drifted, suspended in a warm embrace. The soft hums and gentle murmurs surrounding me were familiar – they belonged to my parents. It was nighttime, the time when our family reunited, nestled within the confines of a cozy bed in a place called home.

One day, I sensed a subtle shift. My mother's heartbeat quickened, and her breath grew shallower. I was aware of the change, even though I couldn't yet comprehend its implications.

The following morning, something extraordinary happened. As my father opened his eyes to greet the new day, he felt a strange sensation – a mix of joy and unease stirring within him. He lay there, gazing at my mother, his dear wife, who continued to sleep peacefully beside him.

In that moment, the knowledge that had lain dormant within my father was awakened. It was the family gift he carried – the premonition of his own demise. But as he looked upon my sleeping mother, it became apparent that this premonition would not be solely his burden anymore.

As the days passed, I continued to grow stronger within my mother's womb. And with each passing day, my father's worry and discomfort grew. He didn't understand why he felt this way – after all, I was a part of him, a part of our family. But the gift he carried warned him that one day, his presence would be required elsewhere, leaving us behind.

I couldn't help but wonder what it was like on the other side, where my father resided before entering this cozy sanctuary. I heard stories of laughter, love, and adventure – things I longed to experience firsthand. But now that I knew of his impending departure, a sense of urgency filled me. I yearned to connect with him, to learn from him, to be with him one last time before he left us forever.

And so, as the days turned into weeks and weeks into months, my father began to find solace in our shared moments. He would speak to me softly, telling stories of his life, sharing words of wisdom, and whispering sweet nothings that I held close to my heart.

On the day my mother delivered me into the world, my father was by her side, a mix of joy and sadness etched upon his face. He looked at me, this tiny being who would one day carry on our family line, and knew that his time with us was drawing near.

The days following my birth were filled with love and laughter. But I could sense the underlying tension – a weight my father carried like a cloak. I couldn't understand it then, but as I grew older and came to learn more about our family gift, I would come to see that it was the knowledge of his own demise that hung over us all, like a heavy cloud in the sky.

As for me, I held on to every moment with my father, cherishing each memory and soaking up every word he spoke. I knew that one day, he would be called away, leaving us behind. But until then, we were a family – bound by love, fate, and our shared gift. And as I grew older, I would come to learn that the weight my father carried was not a burden but a testament to the strength of our bond.
